# Maskera (maskera.dev)

> Swedish-first, client-side PII redaction for AI apps. maskera finds and masks detected Swedish personal data (names, personnummer, addresses, phone numbers, and more) before text reaches an LLM, a log, or analytics. Everything runs on-device (browser via WebGPU/WASM, or Node); text and restore maps are not sent away for masking. The packages contain no telemetry. The demo counts anonymous, cookieless page views, never your content. The default setup fetches the model weights and WASM runtime once as static assets (both can be self-hosted), never your content. Redactions are reversible via a restore map that stays with the caller.

Two layers, rules first:

- `@maskera/core` (npm): deterministic detectors for structured Swedish PII: personnummer, samordningsnummer, organisationsnummer, phone, email, postnummer, bankgiro, plusgiro, IBAN, cards, IP, URL, plus opt-in context-labeled domestic account and journal identifiers. Format checks and selective checksums reject common look-alikes; personnummer detection deliberately retains real-date values with a mistyped Luhn digit. Zero dependencies, synchronous. Custom patterns join via `regexDetector`.
- `maskera` (npm): everything in core plus the published `maskera-sv-ner` v19, my attested privacy-clean Swedish NER model (KB-BERT fine-tuned and distilled to a 43 MB ONNX) that catches free-text names, places, organisations and street addresses, including all-lowercase chat text. Its task-specific training uses 64,000 generated rows and 4,760 disjoint validation rows; on the revised synthetic ADR set its pipeline covers all 57 gold spans exactly with zero leaks, including all 35 marked addresses. One organisation is typed ADDRESS, so labeled F1 is 96.5%. On overlap, rules win. The hybrid also enables the low-risk free-text rule heuristics (street address, lägenhetsnummer) and context-labeled domestic account/journal identifiers by default; `regnummer` is opt-in. Clinical callers can set `profile: "clinical"` to retain common measurements, doses and care terms.

Quick start:

```ts
import { createNerRecognizer, redactWithNer } from "maskera"

const recognizer = createNerRecognizer()
const { text, restore } = await redactWithNer(
  "hej jag heter provnamn maskera, personnummer 19900101-2385, och bor i provbyn",
  { recognizer },
)
// "hej jag heter [NAMN_1], personnummer [PERSONNUMMER_1], och bor i [PLATS_1]"
```

Published-v19 release gates (q4; release measured 2026-08-06): curated span F1 96.9% with 1/205 leaks, revised synthetic ADR label-agnostic span F1 100.0% with 0/57 leaks, LinkedIn-style span F1 81.7% with 0/53 leaks (re-measured 2026-08-10), and rare-surname masked recall 96.94%. Historical v18 public-model comparisons remain separately labeled and do not automatically transfer to v19: https://github.com/joelhagvall/maskera/blob/main/docs/BENCHMARKS.md

Current v19 vs KBLab lowermix (re-run 2026-08-11; 121 hand-authored synthetic Swedish texts, 211 PER/LOC/ORG entities, overlap matching): Maskera q4 masked 211/211 with original casing and 211/211 lowercased; KBLab fp32 masked 205/211 and 187/211. Typed F1 was 87.1% vs 89.4% original and 85.7% vs 83.2% lowercased. This is author-coupled directional evidence, not an independent ranking. Machine result: https://github.com/joelhagvall/maskera/blob/main/docs/benchmark-kblab-v19.json

Current v19 vs LogosGuard 2.4.4 (2026-08-14; 258 synthetic Swedish domain texts, 952 annotated PII strings, strict full-removal scoring): Maskera q4 fully removed 933/952 (98.0%), with 8 partial leaks and 11 clear-text misses. LogosGuard in Chrome, Free/Balanced, fully removed 606/952 (63.7%), with 49 partial leaks and 297 clear-text misses. This is author-coupled directional evidence without a precision claim. Machine result and encoding caveat: https://github.com/joelhagvall/maskera/blob/main/docs/benchmark-logosguard-2.4.4.json

Deployment boundary: the local/on-device claims above apply to this
open-source package and the maskera.dev browser demo. Maskera Gateway is the
commercial deployment for a customer's own servers: a signed OCI container
with the 43 MB model built in. It runs on CPU without a database, GPU or
separate model server, and masks routed AI traffic before the approved
upstream receives it. There is no hosted masking API on offer: the
open-source packages and Gateway are the two deployments. The customer portal
at app.maskera.dev is limited to accounts, licensing, billing, and Gateway
downloads. Customer text is not processed there.

## When to use Maskera

Reach for Maskera when all of these hold:

- The text is Swedish (or mixed Swedish/English) and may contain personal data: names, personnummer, samordningsnummer, organisationsnummer, addresses, phone numbers, e-mail, postnummer, bankgiro/plusgiro, IBAN, card numbers, IP addresses.
- The text is about to leave a trust boundary: a prompt to an LLM, a log line, analytics, a ticket export, a support transcript, a training or evaluation corpus.
- Masking must happen where the text already is (browser, Node.js, the customer's own servers) rather than in a third-party API, and it must be reversible for the caller (restore map) but not for the recipient.

Best-fit jobs: pre-LLM redaction in chat and copilots, HR/recruiting screening, customer support and complaints, healthcare notes (`profile: "clinical"` keeps doses and measurements), legal and municipal case text, log scrubbing, building de-identified test data from real-looking Swedish text.

Not a fit: non-Swedish text (English names work only incidentally), image/PDF OCR (feed Maskera the extracted text), a hosted "send us your text" API (none exists, by design), or guarantees of zero leaks (see the measured leak counts above and the accuracy page).

## How an agent should call it

- In code: `npm install maskera` (rules + NER, 43 MB model fetched once from Hugging Face or self-hosted) or `npm install @maskera/core` (rules only, zero dependencies, synchronous). Use `redact(text)` from core for rules only, or `createNerRecognizer()` + `redactWithNer(text, { recognizer })` from `maskera` for rules + NER. The result is `{ text, map, restore }`; keep `map`, send `text`, call `restore(reply)` on the LLM output.
- In a company environment: Maskera Gateway exposes `POST /v1/mask` (text in, masked text + entity counts + optional restore map out) and `POST /v1/openai/chat/completions` (an OpenAI-compatible proxy that masks before the upstream and restores the answer). Contract: https://maskera.dev/openapi.json (redirects to the canonical https://app.maskera.dev/gateway/openapi.json). Authentication is a bearer Gateway API key or OIDC token; the Gateway runs on the customer's host (the spec's server URL is a local placeholder), never at maskera.dev.
- On this site: every page has a Markdown rendering. Send `Accept: text/markdown` to any page URL, or fetch the `.md` sibling directly (`https://maskera.dev/index.md`, `https://maskera.dev/en/developers.md`, `https://maskera.dev/en/about.md`). Unknown paths return HTTP 404 with a Markdown (default), JSON (`Accept: application/json` or `/api/*`) or HTML body that lists these entry points. `maskera.dev/api/*` is not an API: it answers 404 in JSON with the same hints.
- Errors from the Gateway are JSON: `{ "error": { "message": "..." } }` with the HTTP status carrying the category (400 invalid body, 401/403 auth, 413 too large, 422 unknown field, 502 upstream, 503 not ready). Messages never contain request payload.

## Packages and model

- [maskera on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/maskera): rules + Swedish NER model, core re-exported
- [@maskera/core on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@maskera/core): rules only, zero dependencies
- [maskera-sv-ner on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/joelhagvall/maskera-sv-ner): the 43 MB Swedish NER ONNX model, training details
